basic_details.scholarship_name: Queen's University Graduate Award & International Doctoral Fellowship in Computing
basic_details.offering_entity: Queen's University (School of Computing & School of Graduate Studies and Postdoctoral Affairs)
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Queen's University Main Campus (Kingston, Ontario, Canada)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Restricted to graduate research programs within the School of Computing: Artificial Intelligence, Biomedical Computing, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Human-Computer Interaction, and Theoretical Computer Science.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: 100% of admitted research-stream graduate students receive guaranteed minimum funding packages (~60 to 80 awards annually)
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open international competition; Pakistani graduates typically secure 5 to 10 fully funded seats annually
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 2 years for MSc thesis; 4 years for PhD, renewed annually subject to satisfactory academic progress

nationality_requirements: Open to international and domestic applicants holding a valid passport
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No age limit specified by Queen's School of Computing.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: For MSc: 4-year Bachelor's degree (16 years education) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related STEM discipline from an HEC-recognized institution with first-class standing (minimum 80% or B+ average; CGPA 3.3/4.0). For PhD: Research Master's degree (18 years education) with A- average (minimum 80% or 3.7/4.0 CGPA) and demonstrable research output.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Queen's evaluates international transcripts on an institutional 4.3 GPA scale. B+ minimum corresponds to ~77-79% on Pakistani marks sheets.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Rigorous undergraduate training in algorithms, discrete mathematics, computer architecture, operating systems, and object-oriented programming.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Final-year students graduating before September (Fall intake) or January (Winter intake) are fully eligible to apply with provisional transcripts.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Industrial or software development experience is valued, but demonstrated academic research potential (publications, capstone projects) carries higher weight.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic overall min 7.0 (no band below 6.5), TOEFL iBT min 88 (writing 24, speaking 22, reading 22, listening 20), or Duolingo min 125. Medium of Instruction letters not accepted.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: None; instruction and research conducted entirely in English.
eligibility_requirements.gender_specific_requirements: None; diversity and women in computing initiatives actively encouraged.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Candidates with accepted publications at top-tier venues (IEEE, ACM, NeurIPS) receive priority faculty matching.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: External tri-council or government scholarship recipients receive supplementary top-ups up to allowable university ceilings.

tuition_fee.details: International tuition fees offset by Queen's Graduate Award (QGA) and International Tuition Support awards (~CAD 14,000 to 16,500/yr).

admission_application_fee.details: School of Graduate Studies non-refundable application fee (CAD 110) paid via credit card.

accommodation.details: Funded from guaranteed living stipend. Student apartments in Kingston (An Clachan, John Orr Tower) or shared student housing average CAD 750 to 1,050/month.

monthly_stipend.details: Guaranteed minimum funding package: MSc minimum CAD 23,000/yr; PhD minimum CAD 25,000 to CAD 28,000/yr (~CAD 2,000 to 2,333/month; ~PKR 400,000 to 466,000/month) delivered through Graduate Teaching Assistantships (GTA) and Graduate Research Assistantships (GRA).

airfare.details: International flights between Pakistan and Canada (Toronto Pearson YYZ or Montreal YUL, then rail/bus to Kingston) are self-funded.

visa_fee.details: Canadian Study Permit fee (CAD 150) and biometrics fee (CAD 85) paid to IRCC.

health_insurance.details: University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) provides comprehensive emergency and basic healthcare, supplemented by the SGPS Supplementary Health & Dental Plan.
health_insurance.amount: Included in standard graduate financial package

food_allowance.details: Groceries and living subsistence covered via bi-weekly graduate stipend disbursements.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: High-performance computational infrastructure, lab hardware, and software licenses provided by the School of Computing.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: School of Graduate Studies conference travel grants (CAD 1,000 to 2,000/yr) plus supervisor research grants for student co-authors presenting at premier computing conferences.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Kingston Transit universal student bus pass included in mandatory student activity fee package.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single leading Canadian research university: Queen's University (Kingston, Ontario, Canada)
participating_institutions: Queen's School of Graduate Studies and Postdoctoral Affairs
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: Top 200 global university (QS World #193, THE #201-250); recognized Canadian research powerhouse in biomedical computing, software analytics, and cybersecurity.
available_majors: MSc / PhD in Computing: Artificial Intelligence & Cognitive Science
MSc / PhD in Computing: Biomedical Computing & Computational Medicine
MSc / PhD in Computing: Cybersecurity, Privacy & Distributed Systems
MSc / PhD in Computing: Software Engineering & Analytics
MSc / PhD in Computing: Human-Computer Interaction
MSc / PhD in Computing: Theoretical Computer Science
university_and_program_options.program_duration: MSc Thesis: 2 years; PhD: 4 years full-time.
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor's (MSc) or Master's (PhD) in Computer Science/STEM with 3.3+ GPA, 2 academic recommendation letters, CV, statement of purpose, supervisor pre-match strongly recommended, and IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL 88.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Biomedical computing and machine learning labs have highest applicant volume; software analytics, theory, and human-computer interaction offer relatively higher admission chances.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Reaching out to prospective faculty supervisors between September and November with a polished CV and specific reference to their published work significantly accelerates admission and guarantees funding.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Queen's School of Graduate Studies Online Application System
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the Queen's Graduate Studies application portal, select School of Computing, choose MSc or PhD thesis route, upload documents, and submit referee details.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1 (September - November): Review faculty research groups in Queen's School of Computing and contact matching supervisors.
Step 2 (October - December): Create an account on the Queen's School of Graduate Studies online portal.
Step 3 (November - January): Upload statement of purpose, CV, transcripts, and register 2 academic referees.
Step 4 (By 15 January): Submit application and pay CAD 110 fee before departmental priority deadline.
Step 5 (February - March): Faculty members conduct virtual interviews and review candidate files.
Step 6 (March - April): Departmental admission letters issued with guaranteed funding package details.
Step 7 (April - June): Apply for Canadian Study Permit via IRCC portal.
Step 8 (September): Arrive in Kingston, Ontario for graduate orientation and assistantship appointment.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated automatic funding: Admitted thesis students are automatically awarded Queen's Graduate Award packages without separate funding application.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Two academic reference letters submitted electronically via Queen's automated referee portal.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of Purpose (1-2 pages): Detail academic background, specific research interests, faculty fit, and post-graduation goals.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Concise 1-2 page research statement outlining problem domain, methodological approach, and relevant Queen's computing labs.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV highlighting publications, software repositories, hackathons, and coursework.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Virtual technical video interview (30-45 minutes) conducted by prospective supervisor focusing on technical background, coding fluency, and research vision.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic (7.0+) or TOEFL iBT (88+) or Duolingo (125+). GRE is NOT required.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Unofficial transcripts uploaded for initial review; official HEC-attested documents submitted upon admission offer.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English translations required for non-English credentials.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: 100% digital submission via the Queen's School of Graduate Studies portal.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Scanned color copies of Bachelor's and Master's degree certificates and consolidated semester transcripts.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Attestation by HEC recommended; provisional transcripts accepted for final-semester students with bona fide letter.

required_documents_checklist.specification: 2-page statement outlining academic background, specific research interests in computing, and alignment with target faculty.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Explicitly identify 2-3 Queen's computing professors whose research papers you have studied and cite relevant methodologies.

required_documents_checklist.specification: 2-page academic CV detailing education, distinctions, software projects, GitHub links, and publications.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Highlight final-year project (FYP), competitive programming accomplishments, and industrial internships.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Two confidential letters from academic professors who can attest to applicant's research intellect and analytical rigor.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Referees must submit letters directly from official university domain email addresses (.edu.pk).

required_documents_checklist.specification: Valid IELTS Academic TRF (min 7.0) or TOEFL iBT score report (min 88) sent electronically via institutional code 0949.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Test must have been taken within 24 months of intended intake date.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Reprint of published conference/journal paper, thesis chapter, or technical whitepaper illustrating research aptitude.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Strongly recommended for PhD candidates to demonstrate mastery of scholarly English.

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Main intake cycle is Fall (September). Winter intake offers very limited funding slots.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 35% (cumulative GPA, performance in advanced computing and mathematics courses)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 30% (prior publications, statement of intent, GitHub repos, FYP quality)
selection_process_and_weights.work_experience_weight: 5% (industry software development or machine learning roles)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 10% (clarity of research focus and departmental fit)
selection_process_and_weights.recommendations_weight: 10% (referee credibility and ranking within student cohort)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: School of Computing Graduate Admissions Committee and individual research lab supervisors.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Two-tiered comprehensive assessment: Departmental Graduate Admissions Committee screens academic credentials and language qualifications, followed by individual faculty PI review and commitment of research funding.

competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~70 fully funded admissions packages awarded annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_global: ~5% to 7% overall admit rate for funded research streams
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~4% to 6% among qualified Pakistani STEM applicants
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Undergraduate degree in CS/SE with top 5-10% standing, solid coding capabilities, 1 research publication or strong thesis, IELTS 7.5.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates of NUST, FAST-NUCES, LUMS, GIKI, UET Lahore, and COMSATS.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Canada, China, India, Pakistan, Iran, United States, Nigeria

fake_websites_and_scams: Unauthorized immigration agents advertising guaranteed admissions to Queen's. Admissions decisions rest exclusively with Queen's faculty and School of Graduate Studies.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: CAD 110 application fee is charged directly by Queen's University. Never pay money to third-party consultants.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Applications found using generic agent-written SOPs or ghostwriters are disqualified immediately.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Canadian Study Permit application and biometrics fees: CAD 235 (~PKR 47,000).
Flight ticket from Pakistan to Toronto Pearson: ~PKR 280,000 to 420,000.
First month's rent security deposit in Kingston: ~CAD 1,000 (~PKR 200,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: CLAIM: A GRE score is mandatory for Queen's computing. (FACT: GRE scores are not required and are not considered by the admissions committee).
CLAIM: Direct contact with faculty is forbidden. (FACT: In the School of Computing, securing an interested faculty member is critical to admission with funding).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Some student forums report minimum GPA as 3.0, but competitive international applicants admitted with funding universally present 3.50+ CGPA.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain minimum overall B average (GPA 3.0 on 4.3 scale) in all graduate credit courses and receive satisfactory annual progress ratings from thesis committee.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time campus residency in Kingston and active participation in lab seminars, research group meetings, and designated teaching assistant duties.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Annual progress report submitted jointly by student and supervisor to the Graduate Committee.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Teaching assistantships are limited to a maximum of 10 hours per week (140 hours per term) to prevent conflict with research progress.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None. International graduates are eligible for Canada's Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) of up to 3 years and Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP) permanent residence pathways.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: No clawback of previously disbursed funding upon standard withdrawal, though remaining fellowship payments cease.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_university: Awards cannot be transferred to other Canadian universities.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Switching research groups requires written mutual consent from former supervisor, new supervisor, and the Graduate Coordinator.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: MSc funding capped at 2 years; PhD funding capped at 4 years. Extensions contingent upon external grants or special departmental TA contracts.
